[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Manual kubectl deployments to Kubernetes clusters create audit trail gaps, configuration drift, deployment inconsistencies across environments, and difficulty tracking "who deployed what when." Imperative deployment approaches (kubectl apply, helm install) lack version control and rollback capabilities.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Implement GitOps deployment pattern where Git repositories serve as the single source of truth for application configurations. ArgoCD continuously monitors Git repositories and automatically synchronizes desired state to Kubernetes clusters, enabling declarative deployments, audit trails, and automated rollback.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Production Kubernetes environments requiring audit trails and change tracking
- Multi-environment deployments (dev/staging/production) requiring consistent promotion workflows
- Organizations requiring approval workflows before production deployments
- Teams needing rapid rollback capabilities for deployment failures
page_texts.7:
[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Audit Trail**: All deployments tracked in Git commit history
- **Declarative**: Desired state declared in Git, ArgoCD ensures actual state matches
- **Automated Sync**: Changes to Git automatically deployed without manual intervention
- **Rollback**: Git revert instantly rolls back failed deployments
- **Security**: No direct kubectl access to production clusters required

page_texts.15:
[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```text
GitOps Deployment Workflow
============================

[ Developer: Code + Manifest Changes ]
       ↓ commits
[ Git Repository: Single Source of Truth ]
       ↓ triggers
[ GitHub Actions: CI Pipeline ]
       ↓ builds/tests
[ Container Registry: ECR ]
       ↓ updates manifest
[ Git Repository: Updated Image Tags ]
       ↓ syncs (3min interval)
[ ArgoCD: Continuous Deployment ]
       ↓ applies
[ Kubernetes Cluster: Target Environment ]
       ↓ monitors
[ ArgoCD: Health Status + Drift Detection ]

Features:

- Automated sync waves for dependencies
- Health checks before progression
- Automatic rollback on failure
- Audit trail via Git history
```

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|-----------|----------------|--------------|
| **Git Repository** | Single source of truth for application manifests | GitHub/GitLab, branch protection |
| **ArgoCD** | Continuous deployment controller monitoring Git | Kubernetes cluster, Git access |
| **Application CRD** | Defines application source, destination, sync policy | ArgoCD installation |
| **ApplicationSet** | Template for multi-environment deployments | ArgoCD ApplicationSet controller |
| **Sync Waves** | Coordinate multi-service deployment ordering | ArgoCD sync hooks |

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

**Organizational Readiness:**

- Development teams trained on Git workflows (branching, PRs, merges)
- Agreement on Git repository structure and branching strategy
- Defined promotion process (dev → staging → production)
- Code review culture established

**Technical Requirements:**

- EKS cluster for ArgoCD installation (or use existing management cluster)
- Git repository hosting (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)
- Container registry (ECR) for application images
- Helm >= 3.0 or Kustomize >= 4.0
- CI/CD pipeline for container builds (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI)

**Tooling:**

- kubectl, argocd CLI, helm CLI
- Git client with SSH key authentication
- AWS credentials with EKS cluster access

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#phase-1-deploy-argocd-week-1]

#### Phase 1: Deploy ArgoCD (Week 1)

**1.1 Install ArgoCD with High Availability**

```bash
# Create namespace
kubectl create namespace argocd

# Install ArgoCD (HA mode)
kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml

# Or install via Helm with custom values
helm repo add argo https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm
helm repo update

cat > argocd-values.yaml <<EOF
server:
  replicas: 2
  service:
    type: LoadBalancer
    annotations:
      service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb
      service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "true"

  # SSO configuration (Okta)
  config:
    url: https://argocd.gainwell.com
    oidc.config: |
      name: Okta
      issuer: https://gainwell.okta.com
      clientID: \$oidc.okta.clientId
      clientSecret: \$oidc.okta.clientSecret
      requestedScopes:
        - openid
        - profile
        - email
        - groups

  rbacConfig:
    policy.default: role:readonly
    policy.csv: |
      p, role:org-admin, applications, *, */*, allow
      p, role:org-admin, clusters, get, *, allow
      p, role:org-admin, repositories, get, *, allow
      g, gainwell-platform-team, role:admin
      g, gainwell-developers, role:org-admin

repoServer:
  replicas: 2

controller:
  replicas: 2

applicationSet:
  enabled: true

notifications:
  enabled: true
  argocdUrl: https://argocd.gainwell.com
  notifiers:
    service.slack: |
      token: \$slack-token
  templates:
    template.app-deployed: |
      message: |
        Application {{.app.metadata.name}} deployed to {{.app.spec.destination.namespace}}
        Sync Status: {{.app.status.sync.status}}
        Health: {{.app.status.health.status}}
  triggers:
    trigger.on-deployed: |
      - when: app.status.sync.status == 'Synced'
        send: [app-deployed]
EOF

helm install argocd argo/argo-cd \

  --namespace argocd \
  --values argocd-values.yaml
```

**1.2 Configure Ingress/ALB**

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: argocd-server
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internal
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-type: ip
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: HTTPS
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/xxx
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTPS":443}]'
spec:
  ingressClassName: alb
  rules:

  - host: argocd.gainwell.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: argocd-server
            port:
              number: 443
```

**1.3 Access ArgoCD UI**

```bash
# Get initial admin password
kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret \

  -o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 -d

# Port-forward for initial access
kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443

# Login via CLI
argocd login localhost:8080 --username admin --password <password>

# Change admin password
argocd account update-password
```

#### Phase 2: Repository Structure (Week 1-2)

**2.1 Git Repository Organization**

**Option A: Monorepo (Recommended for smaller orgs)**

```text
k8s-applications/
├── apps/
│   ├── claims-service/
│   │   ├── base/
│   │   │   ├── deployment.yaml
│   │   │   ├── service.yaml
│   │   │   └── kustomization.yaml
│   │   ├── overlays/
│   │   │   ├── dev/
│   │   │   │   └── kustomization.yaml
│   │   │   ├── staging/
│   │   │   │   └── kustomization.yaml
│   │   │   └── production/
│   │   │       └── kustomization.yaml
│   │   └── helm/
│   │       ├── Chart.yaml
│   │       ├── values.yaml
│   │       ├── values-staging.yaml
│   │       └── values-production.yaml
│   └── eligibility-service/
├── argocd-apps/
│   ├── claims-service-dev.yaml
│   ├── claims-service-staging.yaml
│   └── claims-service-production.yaml
└── README.md
```

**Option B: Repository per Application (Larger teams)**

```text
claims-service-deployment/
├── kubernetes/
│   ├── base/
│   └── overlays/
│       ├── dev/
│       ├── staging/
│       └── production/
└── helm/
```

**2.2 Example Application Manifest (Helm)**

```yaml
# helm/values.yaml (base values)
replicaCount: 2

image:
  repository: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-service
  tag: "1.0.0"  # Overridden by CI/CD
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 80
  targetPort: 8080

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: alb
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internal
  hosts:
    - host: claims.example.com
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix

resources:
  requests:
    memory: "512Mi"
    cpu: "500m"
  limits:
    memory: "1Gi"
    cpu: "1000m"

autoscaling:
  enabled: true
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
```

```yaml
# helm/values-production.yaml (production overrides)
replicaCount: 6

autoscaling:
  minReplicas: 6
  maxReplicas: 30

resources:
  requests:
    memory: "1Gi"
    cpu: "1000m"
  limits:
    memory: "2Gi"
    cpu: "2000m"

ingress:
  hosts:
    - host: claims.gainwell.com
```

**2.3 Example Application Manifest (Kustomize)**

```yaml
# base/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: claims-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: claims-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: claims-service
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: claims-service-sa

      # Pod-level security context (recommended)
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10000
        fsGroup: 10000
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault

      containers:
      - name: claims-service
        image: claims-service:latest

        # Container-level security context
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10000
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080

        volumeMounts:
        - name: tmp
          mountPath: /tmp

        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          limits:
            memory: "1Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"

      volumes:
      - name: tmp
        emptyDir: {}
```

```yaml
# overlays/production/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

namespace: production

resources:

- ../../base

replicas:

- name: claims-service
  count: 6

images:

- name: claims-service
  newName: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/claims-service
  newTag: v1.2.3

patchesStrategicMerge:

- deployment-patch.yaml
```

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#phase-3-application-onboarding-week-2-3]

#### Phase 3: Application Onboarding (Week 2-3)

**3.1 Create ArgoCD Application**

```yaml
# argocd-apps/claims-service-production.yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: claims-service-production
  namespace: argocd
  finalizers:

  - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
spec:
  project: default

  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/gainwell/k8s-applications
    targetRevision: main
    path: apps/claims-service/helm
    helm:
      releaseName: claims-service
      valueFiles:
      - values.yaml
      - values-production.yaml

  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: production

  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
      allowEmpty: false

    syncOptions:
    - CreateNamespace=false  # Namespace pre-created
    - PrunePropagationPolicy=foreground
    - PruneLast=true

    retry:
      limit: 5
      backoff:
        duration: 5s
        factor: 2
        maxDuration: 3m
```

**3.2 Apply Application to ArgoCD**

```bash
# Apply Application manifest
kubectl apply -f argocd-apps/claims-service-production.yaml

# Or create via CLI
argocd app create claims-service-production \

  --repo https://github.com/gainwell/k8s-applications \
  --path apps/claims-service/helm \
  --dest-server https://kubernetes.default.svc \
  --dest-namespace production \
  --helm-set image.tag=v1.2.3 \
  --sync-policy automated \
  --auto-prune \
  --self-heal
```

**3.3 Configure Sync Waves for Ordered Deployment**

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: database-schema
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "0"  # Deploy first

---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: database-migration
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "1"  # Deploy second
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: claims-service
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "2"  # Deploy last
```

#### Phase 4: ApplicationSets for Multi-Environment (Week 3-4)

**4.1 ApplicationSet for All Environments**

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: claims-service
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  generators:

  - list:
      elements:
      - environment: dev
        cluster: https://dev-cluster.example.com
        namespace: dev
        replicas: "2"
        syncAuto: "true"
      - environment: staging
        cluster: https://staging-cluster.example.com
        namespace: staging
        replicas: "4"
        syncAuto: "true"
      - environment: production
        cluster: https://prod-cluster.example.com
        namespace: production
        replicas: "6"
        syncAuto: "false"  # Manual sync for production

  template:
    metadata:
      name: 'claims-service-{{environment}}'
    spec:
      project: default
      source:
        repoURL: https://github.com/gainwell/k8s-applications
        targetRevision: main
        path: apps/claims-service/helm
        helm:
          valueFiles:
          - values.yaml
          - 'values-{{environment}}.yaml'
          parameters:
          - name: replicaCount
            value: '{{replicas}}'

      destination:
        server: '{{cluster}}'
        namespace: '{{namespace}}'

      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: '{{syncAuto}}'
        syncOptions:
        - CreateNamespace=false
```

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#phase-5-cicd-integration-week-4]

#### Phase 5: CI/CD Integration (Week 4)

**5.1 GitHub Actions Workflow for Image Build + GitOps Update**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yaml
name: Build and Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - develop

env:
  ECR_REGISTRY: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
  ECR_REPOSITORY: claims-service

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image-tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Docker metadata
      id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
      with:
        images: ${{ env.ECR_REGISTRY }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}
        tags: |
          type=sha,prefix={{branch}}-
          type=semver,pattern={{version}}

    - name: Configure AWS credentials
      uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
      with:
        role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GithubActionsRole
        aws-region: us-east-1

    - name: Login to ECR
      uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

  update-gitops:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout GitOps repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        repository: gainwell/k8s-applications
        token: ${{ secrets.GITOPS_PAT }}

    - name: Update image tag
      run: |
        # Update Helm values
        yq e -i '.image.tag = "${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }}"' \
          apps/claims-service/helm/values-${{ github.ref_name }}.yaml

        # Or update Kustomize
        cd apps/claims-service/overlays/${{ github.ref_name }}
        kustomize edit set image claims-service=${{ env.ECR_REGISTRY }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }}

    - name: Commit and push
      run: |
        git config user.name "GitHub Actions"
        git config user.email "actions@github.com"
        git add .
        git commit -m "Update claims-service to ${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }}"
        git push
```

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

1. **Separate Repositories**: Application code in one repo, Kubernetes manifests in another (separation of concerns)
2. **Environment Branches or Overlays**: Use Kustomize overlays or Helm values for environment-specific configurations
3. **Automated Sync for Non-Prod**: Enable automated sync for dev/staging; manual sync for production
4. **Sync Waves**: Use ArgoCD sync waves (`argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave`) for ordered multi-resource deployments
5. **Health Checks**: Define custom health checks for CRDs ensuring ArgoCD correctly detects application health
6. **Git Commit Messages**: Include ticket references (JIRA-123) for audit traceability
7. **Branch Protection**: Require PR reviews for production branches preventing direct commits
8. **ArgoCD Projects**: Use ArgoCD Projects to isolate team access to specific applications/namespaces
9. **Notifications**: Configure Slack/email notifications for sync failures and health degradations
10. **Secrets Management**: Never commit secrets; use External Secrets Operator or Sealed Secrets
11. **Application Cleanup**: Set `prune: true` for automatic removal of deleted resources
12. **Diff Before Sync**: Always review ArgoCD diff before syncing production changes
13. **Rollback Strategy**: Document rollback procedures (Git revert, manual sync to previous commit)
14. **Resource Hooks**: Use ArgoCD hooks (PreSync, Sync, PostSync) for database migrations and smoke tests

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

1. **Secrets in Git**
   - **Problem**: Committing secrets to Git creates security vulnerability
   - **Solution**: Use External Secrets Operator syncing from AWS Secrets Manager, or Sealed Secrets for encrypted secrets in Git

2. **Missing Health Checks**
   - **Problem**: ArgoCD marks application healthy before pods ready, causing premature sync completion
   - **Solution**: Implement readiness probes on all pods; define custom health checks for CRDs

3. **Overly Complex Kustomize**
   - **Problem**: Deep overlay hierarchies difficult to debug and maintain
   - **Solution**: Keep Kustomize overlays shallow (2 levels max); prefer Helm for complex configurations

4. **Inadequate RBAC**
   - **Problem**: All developers have cluster-admin access via ArgoCD
   - **Solution**: Use ArgoCD Projects with namespace-scoped RBAC; integrate with SSO/OIDC

5. **No Automated Testing**
   - **Problem**: Invalid YAML committed to Git causes ArgoCD sync failures
   - **Solution**: CI pipeline with kubeval/kubeconform validating manifests before merge

6. **Ignoring Sync Failures**
   - **Problem**: ArgoCD sync failures go unnoticed, application remains out-of-sync
   - **Solution**: Configure ArgoCD notifications, monitor sync status in dashboards

7. **Large Monorepo Performance**
   - **Problem**: Single repo with 100+ applications slows Git operations
   - **Solution**: Split into multiple repos by portfolio or team

8. **Drift from Manual Changes**
   - **Problem**: Developers run kubectl commands bypassing GitOps, creating drift
   - **Solution**: Enable selfHeal, restrict kubectl access to production, enforce GitOps-only policy

9. **Missing Rollback Testing**
   - **Problem**: Git revert works but application doesn't roll back correctly
   - **Solution**: Regularly test rollback procedures, ensure database migrations are reversible

10. **Sync Wave Mistakes**
    - **Problem**: Application pods start before database migration completes
    - **Solution**: Carefully order sync waves (migrations wave 0, apps wave 1); test ordering

### Compliance Requirements

**GitOps Standards:**

- All production deployments via GitOps (no direct kubectl)
- Git commit messages include ticket references
- Branch protection enforcing code review for production
- Audit logs retained for regulatory compliance

**Security Requirements (Recommended):**

- All manifests in Git must comply with Pod Security Standards (Restricted)
- Admission policies enforce security controls before deployment (PTN-SEC-K8S-002)
- Container images referenced in manifests must be signed and scanned
- Secrets managed via External Secrets Operator, not hardcoded in Git (PTN-SEC-K8S-003)
- NetworkPolicies defined alongside application manifests
- SecurityContext enforced in all Deployment/StatefulSet/Job templates

**Note:** GitOps provides complete audit trail of all configuration changes through Git history, essential for HIPAA compliance and security incident investigation.

### Real-World Example 1: Multi-Environment Promotion Pipeline

**Context**: Claims processing microservice deployed across dev, staging, and production environments with progressive promotion.

**Implementation**: ApplicationSet-based deployment with automated dev/staging sync and manual production approval. Developer commits trigger CI/CD pipeline building container images and updating GitOps repository. ArgoCD monitors Git and syncs changes within 3 minutes.

- Deployment time reduced from 30-60 minutes to 3-5 minutes per environment
- Complete audit trail via Git history
- Zero configuration drift between environments
- 2-minute rollback capability via Git revert

**Context**: Production deployment introduces critical bug affecting 10% of transactions.

[patterns/infrastructure/kubernetes/PTN-INFRA-K8S-003-infrastructure-gitops-deployment-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Manual kubectl deployments lack audit trails, create configuration drift between environments, and complicate rollback procedures. Imperative approaches don't provide version control for infrastructure changes.

**Solution:** Implement GitOps deployment pattern using ArgoCD monitoring Git repositories as single source of truth. Git commits automatically trigger deployments, providing declarative infrastructure, complete audit trails, and instant rollback capability via Git revert.

**When to Use:** Production Kubernetes environments requiring audit trails, multi-environment consistency (dev/staging/prod), compliance with change management policies, and rapid rollback capabilities.

**Key Benefits:**

- **Complete Audit Trail**: Git history documents all deployments with committer identity and timestamps
- **Automated Deployments**: Git commits trigger automated sync within 3 minutes
- **Instant Rollback**: Git revert enables 2-5 minute recovery from failed deployments
- **Zero Configuration Drift**: ArgoCD ensures actual state matches desired Git state
- **Security**: No direct kubectl access to production clusters required

**Implementation Complexity:** Low-Medium (ArgoCD installation straightforward, repository organization requires planning)

**Prerequisites:**

- ArgoCD or Flux CD deployed
- Git repositories with branch protection
- Helm charts or Kustomize overlays for environment-specific configurations
- CI/CD pipeline for container image builds

**Key Metrics:**

- Deployment time: 3-5 minutes (90% faster than manual)
- Rollback time: 2-5 minutes (85% faster than manual)
- Configuration drift: 0% (GitOps-enforced)
- Deployment error rate: 2% (87% reduction via CI validation)

**Related Patterns:** Multi-Cluster Management, Platform-as-a-Product, Secrets Management, Microservices Architecture
